USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold the current tariff posture but use the scheduled Trump–Xi meeting at the G20 in Osaka (late June) as an off-ramp to restart substantive negotiations rather than escalating to the threatened $300B tranche. Keep List 3 at 25% and the Huawei entity list in place as leverage, but signal a credible path to de-escalation on enforcement and purchases so we reach a framework deal without triggering China's rare-earth retaliation.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat to US interests is material and rising (threat_score +0.45). The bond market is flashing a hard recession warning before the decision date: the 10Y yield fell from ~2.85% (Dec) to 2.12% and the 2Y to 1.83% by June 5, inverting the 10Y-3M curve, while WTI slid from ~$66 to ~$51.5 — all knowable signals of growth/risk stress from the May escalation (List 3 raised to 25% on May 10, Huawei entity-listed May 16, China's $60B retaliation effective June 1). Politically, China's shutdown of the agriculture market forced a $16B farm bailout (May 23), with soybean exports down ~50%, putting Trump's own farm-belt base under strain and fueling domestic political pressure. China's rare-earth counter-leverage threat (state media, May 29) exposes genuine US electronics/defense supply-chain vulnerability, and PIIE estimates put the full-tariff household cost at ~$2,200/yr. That is why I do NOT recommend further escalation: adding the $300B tranche and taxing essentially all Chinese imports would hit US consumers directly and invite rare-earth retaliation at a moment when the yield curve already signals recession risk. The high threat argues for de-escalation, not more pressure. With a presidential G20 meeting already on the calendar, the disciplined move is to negotiate a deal while retaining tariffs as enforcement leverage — hence action_score +0.2 / 'negotiate'.

CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Maintain our current retaliatory posture and keep the door open for negotiation, using the late-June G20 meeting as the leverage rather than escalating or conceding now. We should not initiate further tariff or entity-list escalation, which would only invite the threatened $300B tranche and deeper tech decapitation; but we should also not roll back our $60B retaliation or Huawei-related measures, which would reward Washington's gambit and undercut domestic resolve. Signal readiness to return to the table at Osaka while holding firm on Huawei.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat reading is driven by the two-track escalation visible in the timeline: on May 10 the US raised List 3 tariffs from 10% to 25% on ~$200B and directed preparation of tariffs on the remaining ~$300B, and on May 16 it placed Huawei and 70 affiliates on the Entity List, with Google suspending Android/GMS and US chip suppliers pausing sales (May 20). This is precisely the 'firm-level targeting (Huawei) + major export sectors hit + FX pressure' cluster of the +0.5 CHN anchor. FX confirms the bite: the yuan has depreciated ~2.7-2.9% since Trump's May 5 tweet and sits near 6.91-6.94, within reach of the psychologically critical 7.0 level. Talks are stalled — no US negotiators scheduled to come to Beijing — and the G20 is a binary, risky window. Yet the threat is not existential: China retains ample reserves (defending the 7 line), has responding leverage (rare-earth readiness signalled by Xi's Jiangxi visit, the May 31 'unreliable entity list'), and nationalistic mobilization is strengthening, not weakening, regime standing. This justifies a high-but-not-existential ~+0.55. For action, escalation would be self-defeating — it would trigger the full $300B tranche and widen allied tech pressure (SoftBank already snubbing Huawei), deepening harm to an already-strained export economy; concession would reward the Huawei decapitation and erode credibility. The correct stance is to hold and negotiate toward de-escalation at the G20, where Trump faces domestic market pain (10Y yield plunged to ~2.12, 2Y to ~1.83, oil below $52, VIX elevated — US markets pricing recession risk) and farm-belt pressure that make a truce attainable on better terms.
